title: Support vector machine predicts drug binding to cucurbit[7]uril, tested experimentally
summary: A kernel support vector machine trained on density functional theory data was used to predict small-molecule binding to cucurbit[7]uril (CB[7]). The abstract says it may confer some predictive ability; it predicted strong binding for TAK-580 and poor binding for selumetinib, and experiments confirmed both. Selumetinib was found to bind the larger cucurbit[8]uril. Only two drugs were tested.
ai_technology: Support vector machine regression trained on DFT-derived data

evidence.tested: Experimental binding of two drugs (TAK-580 and selumetinib) predicted by the model, plus mass transfer simulations.
evidence.unknown: Only two drugs tested; predictive ability described as modest; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Support vector machine predicting host-guest binding coefficients from DFT training data.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref where stated. Publisher full text not accessed.
